entities.summary: Timor-Leste is a sovereign nation in Southeast Asia, Asia. Its capital is Dili. Official languages include Portuguese, Tetum. Government: Unitary parliamentary republic. Population: approximately 1.4 million. Area: 14,919 km². Comprehensive index for Timor-Leste (East Timor) covering indigenous Papuan/Austronesian peoples, sandalwood trade, Portuguese colonization 1515, Dutch West Timor division, Japanese WWII occupation, Indonesian invasion 1975 (post-Portuguese withdrawal), Santa Cruz massacre 1991, independence referendum 1999 (78.5% yes, violence by Indonesian militias), UN transitional administration (UNTAET), full independence 2002, 2006 crisis, Xanana Gusmão leadership, oil/gas revenues (Timor Sea), and youngest 21st century nation-state.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Timor-Leste's independence referendum in 1999 resulted in a 78.5% yes vote, despite violence by Indonesian militias, and its full independence in 2002 marked the end of colonial rule and the beginning of a new era for the island nation.
